text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Sunday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Israel Air Force strikes at Hizbollah targets in Lebanon.
- Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu: "We'll hit back strongly against Hizbollah.
- Islamic Jihad: More suicide attacks soon.
- Ilan Biran, former army central commander, named defence ministry director-general.
- Israeli security cabinet signs declaration of secrecy.
- Yom Kippur starts tonight; complete Israeli shutdown for 25 hours.
HAARETZ
- Netanyahu, Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai will decide soon whether to go on reinforcing Israeli troops on the Golan.
- Turkish President Demirel tells Haaretz in interview that the military cooperation with Israel will continue without disturbance.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai in interview tells Syrian President Hafez al-Assad: "Come let's take a different direction.
- 73 percent of Israeli Jews fast on Yom Kippur and 69 percent go to synagogue, poll shows.
MAARIV
- Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel expected to announce fall in interest rate by half a percentage point on Tuesday.
- Mordechai says: "There's a drop in tensions with Syria. We're following closely what's happening.
- Police on high alert for Yom Kippur.
- Qatar delays opening of its interest section in Israel.

- Poll of 605 Israelis on Thursday shows 48 percent would pick Ehud Barak of Labour compared to 40 percent for Netanyahu in elections for prime minister today. Asked which of four people was best suited to be Labour party leader and candidate for prime minister, 40 percent said Barak, 15 percent Haim Ramon, 11 percent Uzi Baram and 4 percent Ephraim Sneh.
